free_tier.stated: Open data with no fee, no key and no registration: forecasts, alerts and observations for the United States from api.weather.gov; a User-Agent header is required and the request rate limit is not published.
free_tier.notes: Station observations are kept for 7 days and alerts for 7 days; a point outside the United States answers HTTP 404. Bulk path: the NOMADS server (120 hits a minute per IP address, counted across the NCEP hosts) and the NOAA Open Data Dissemination buckets on cloud platforms, open to the public; NWS alert archives are held by NCEI.

retention.stated: station observations are retained for 7 days and alerts for the past 7 days

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at api.weather.gov (GeoJSON, JSON-LD, DWML, CAP and ATOM by the Accept header); an OpenAPI 3.1 specification is published at api.weather.gov/openapi.json
tooling: any HTTP client that sets a User-Agent; OpenAPI specification for generated clients
chaining: A keyless official US forecast and alert source; pair with api.met.no for coordinates outside the United States and with NOAA's NODD buckets for model files.

limits.value: unverified: the rate limit is not published; over it the API answers an error that can be retried after the limit clears, typically within 5 seconds

binding_note: The only stated limit is the unpublished request rate.

identity_cost.detail: No sign-up and no key: a User-Agent string, which can be anything and may carry a contact, is the only identification; the vendor plans to replace it with an API key.

reliability_note: A request without a User-Agent answers HTTP 403; over the unpublished limit the API errors and recovers after about 5 seconds.
confidence_note: Terms are read from first-party pages; keyless points and forecast calls answered HTTP 200 and a non-US point answered HTTP 404; the rate limit was not driven.

evidence.proved: the API is open data with no fee
evidence.quote: All of the information presented via the API is intended to be open data, free to use for any purpose.
The rate limit is not public information, but allows a generous amount for typical use.

evidence.proved: over the limit a request errors and can be retried, typically within 5 seconds
evidence.quote: If the rate limit is execeed a request will return with an error, and may be retried after the limit clears (typically within 5 seconds).

evidence.proved: a User-Agent is the only identification
evidence.quote: A User Agent is required to identify your application.
This will be replaced with an API key in the future.
Note: since this service is designed for realtime data, only 7 days of observations are retained for weather stations.
The /alerts endpoint contains alerts issued over the past seven days.

evidence.proved: the User-Agent string does not change limits
evidence.quote: The API remains open and free to use and there are no limits imposed based on the User-Agent string.

evidence.proved: a request without a User-Agent answers 403
evidence.quote: Make sure your program is including a `User-Agent` header in your request.
